headline: France's 10-year tops 5% for the first time since 2002; oil gives back a $2 spike to end flat
summary: Crude jumped about $2 early as Iran ruled out talks and US stocks fell more than expected, then gave it all back on Russia–Ukraine peace-talk progress: Brent settled flat at $108.82 and December WTI fell 0.7% to $97.15, while RBOB edged up to $3.1205. Gold held near $4,130 after a one-week low and silver slipped. France dominated bonds as the 10-year OAT closed above 5% and the spread to Bunds neared 160bp; Treasuries ended slightly higher in yield after a mixed 20-year auction.
drivers: The 10-year OAT closed near 5.01%, up about 8–9bp and the highest since July 2002, as weekend riots, fresh protests called for Saturday and a stalled 2027 budget hit French debt. The OAT–Bund spread widened toward 158bp, close to early October's 15-year high, while Bunds rose only about 3bp.
Oil: two peace tracks vs tight stocks

Iran said there could be no dialogue with the US while blockaded, lifting WTI to $99.95 and Brent to $110.85, and the EIA showed a 3.1M-barrel crude draw against about 0.3M expected. Putin agreeing to resume US-mediated Ukraine talks next month erased the gains; WTI later rose above $98 after the close on a report of Gulf embassy evacuations.

Treasury sold $13B of 20-year bonds at 5.469%, the highest clearing yield since 1986, with a 2.73 bid-to-cover; analysts called it mixed. At the 3pm close the 2-year rose about 4bp to 4.82% and the 10-year about 3bp to 5.145%, with an October hike priced near 15% but three hikes over 12 months.
Metals stuck between oil and the Fed

Gold touched its lowest since Oct 15 as the morning oil spike revived inflation and hike worries, then recovered as crude faded; December futures settled 0.2% higher at $4,150. Silver lagged, down about 0.5% near $57.6, as profit-taking followed Tuesday's gain.

oil.note: Dec WTI settled down $0.67 (-0.7%) at $97.15 after a $99.95 high; Brent flat at $108.82.
oil.why: Crude rallied about $2 early after Iran's president said there could be no talks while the US blockades the country, more ships were hit near Hormuz, and the EIA reported a 3.1M-barrel crude draw against a 0.3M forecast. The gains faded when the Kremlin said Putin would resume US-mediated Ukraine talks next month, raising hopes for Russian diesel supply. A 1M-barrel Cushing build kept WTI weaker than Brent, widening the spread past $11.
oil.outlook: Firm but headline-driven: Brent $105–112 and WTI $94–101, with dips bought while Hormuz stays disrupted and US stocks sit 3% below average. A credible US–Iran opening would break the floor; a close above $112 Brent would target $115.
oil.watch: Gulf embassy evacuation reports, Hormuz shipping, the Oct 28 EIA report and OPEC+ on Nov 1.

gas.note: RBOB Nov rose 0.33¢ (+0.1%) to $3.1205, ending a two-day slide; AAA pump average $4.26.
gas.why: Gasoline steadied after two days of losses as the EIA showed stocks down 3.0M barrels against an expected flat reading, leaving them 5% below the five-year average, and implied demand jumped by 575,000 b/d to about 9.0M b/d. That offset crude's late fade. Diesel fell instead, about 7–11¢, after a distillate build and a US plan to lend 315,000 barrels from the Northeast heating-oil reserve.
gas.outlook: Range $3.00–3.25. Tight stocks support it, but the winter-blend switch and falling pump prices limit upside; a break above $3.30 would need a new crude spike.
gas.watch: The Nov RBOB expiry on Oct 30, EIA data Oct 28 and pump prices, now down 7¢ in a week.

gold.note: Spot near $4,130, little changed after a one-week low; Dec futures settled up 0.2% at $4,150.
gold.why: Gold slipped to its lowest since Oct 15 in the morning as oil's spike revived inflation fears and kept a December Fed hike in play, with markets pricing three hikes over the next year. It recovered as crude reversed and the dollar index held near 101.5. Defensive demand on Gulf security limits the downside, but 5%-plus Treasury yields keep drawing money away from bullion.
gold.outlook: Range $4,080–4,200 into the Oct 28 Fed, slight downside tilt while real yields stay high. A close above $4,180 would turn it up; below $4,080 opens $4,050.
gold.watch: Oil and Gulf headlines, Thursday's jobless claims and the Fed on Oct 28.

silver.note: Spot about $57.6, down roughly 0.5%; gold/silver ratio near 72.
silver.why: Silver gave back part of Tuesday's 1.5% rebound as traders took profits and the morning oil spike pushed up rate-hike worries. Its industrial side kept it more sensitive than gold to growth concerns. The late fall in crude and a steady dollar trimmed the losses, and it held above Monday's $56.70 low.
silver.outlook: Range $56.30–59.00 with no clear trend. A close above $58.80 would target $60; a break below $56.30 would reopen the July lows.
silver.watch: Risk appetite, the dollar, China data and the Fed on Oct 28.

us2y.note: Rose about 4bp to near 4.82% at the 3pm close, its biggest daily rise since Sept 28.
us2y.why: The 2-year led the curve higher as the morning oil jump kept inflation risk in view, with CPI near 3.7%. Markets still give an October hike only about a 15% chance but fully price three hikes over 12 months. Late in the day it eased toward 4.81% as haven buying returned after a report of Gulf embassy evacuations.
us2y.outlook: Range 4.72–4.88% until the Fed. A hawkish statement or strong data tests 4.88%; a dovish hold that cuts December odds would bring 4.72%.
us2y.watch: Jobless claims Thursday, the Fed on Oct 27–28 and October jobs data.

us5y.note: About 4.95–4.98%, a few bp higher with the front end.
us5y.why: The 5-year rose with the 2-year as oil's early spike revived inflation concerns and steady hike pricing anchored the belly near 5%. Thursday's $26 billion 5-year TIPS auction added supply pressure, while late haven buying on Gulf headlines pared the move.
us5y.outlook: Range 4.88–5.05%. A clear December hike signal from the Fed would push it through 5%; a drop in oil would pull it back below 4.90%.
us5y.watch: The 5-year TIPS sale Oct 22, oil and the Fed on Oct 28.

us10y.note: Up about 3bp to 5.145% at the 3pm close (Tradeweb), easing toward 5.12% late.
us10y.why: The 10-year swung both ways: it hit 5.08% in the morning as AI-stock worries drove haven demand, then rose after a mixed 20-year auction that cleared at 5.469%, the highest since 1986, with a 2.73 bid-to-cover. Oil's early jump and steady hike pricing added to the rise. After the close, a Gulf embassy evacuation report sent buyers back in.
us10y.outlook: Range 5.05–5.25%. Supply and oil near $100 keep a floor; a dovish Fed or weak data could test 5.05%, while a close above 5.25% would reopen this month's 5.31% high.
us10y.watch: 5-year TIPS auction Oct 22, jobless claims, the Fed on Oct 28 and the Nov 4 refunding.

us30y.note: About 5.44% at the 3pm close, up roughly 1bp; the curve flattened as the short end led.
us30y.why: The 30-year rose less than the front end as the 20-year auction drew better demand than September's weak sale, even at a 5.469% clearing yield. Hopes that Treasury trims long-bond sizes at the Nov 4 refunding and a softer late tone on Gulf headlines kept the long end steady.
us30y.outlook: Range 5.35–5.55%. Smaller long-bond auctions would flatten the curve further; no change at the refunding would push term premium higher.
us30y.watch: The Nov 4 refunding and the Fed on Oct 28.

de2y.why: The Schatz rose as oil's early spike reinforced views that energy-driven inflation, with euro-area CPI at 3.8%, keeps further ECB tightening on the table. Markets see almost no chance of a move on Oct 29 but still lean toward a hike by December from the 2.50% deposit rate.
de2y.outlook: Range 3.00–3.15%. Firm ECB guidance on Oct 29 would lift it toward 3.15%; a drop in oil would pull it back near 3.00%.
de2y.watch: ECB decision Oct 29 and flash October inflation.

de5y.note: Near 3.21–3.22%, a couple of bp higher.
de5y.why: The 5-year Bund rose with the wider euro-area selloff as energy costs and ECB hike bets offset haven demand. Investors bought German debt over French, which limited the rise, but not enough to pull yields lower as France's spread widened.
de5y.outlook: Range 3.12–3.30% into the ECB. More French stress keeps a lid on it; a hawkish ECB or oil rebound would lift it.
de5y.watch: ECB Oct 29, oil and the OAT–Bund spread.

de10y.note: Up about 3bp to near 3.43%, near the middle of this month's range.
de10y.why: The 10-year Bund rose with global yields and oil's early jump, but haven buying from the French selloff kept it far behind OATs, so the spread widened to about 158bp. Reuters put it up 3bp at 3.426%. The gap to Treasuries stayed near 170bp, reflecting higher US policy rates.
de10y.outlook: Range 3.35–3.55%. French stress and softer oil cap it; a move above 3.50% would need a hawkish ECB or a new oil spike.
de10y.watch: ECB Oct 29, French protests Saturday and German supply.

de30y.note: About 3.78%, a little higher; the long end tracked global yields.
de30y.why: The 30-year Bund edged up with US long bonds after the 20-year Treasury auction and oil's early rise. The move was smaller than in France, where the long end carries a fiscal premium, as German long debt continues to attract haven demand.
de30y.outlook: Range 3.70–3.90%. It follows US long bonds more than the ECB.
de30y.watch: US long-end yields, the Nov 4 refunding and German long-dated sales.

fr2y.note: About 3.72%, up roughly 1–2bp; short OATs held better than longer maturities.
fr2y.why: The 2-year OAT rose modestly as short French paper still tracks ECB pricing more than fiscal risk. Even so, it trades about 60bp over the Schatz, a sign that the political premium is creeping into shorter maturities as protests spread and the budget stalls.
fr2y.outlook: Range 3.62–3.80%; it would jump only if a censure motion brought down the government.
fr2y.watch: Protests on Saturday Oct 24, the budget debate from Oct 27 and the ECB on Oct 29.

fr5y.note: About 4.39%, up roughly 3–4bp as France sold off across the curve.
fr5y.why: The 5-year OAT rose as investors weighed weekend riots, a new round of protests called for Saturday and a revenue vote that failed to reassure. Doubts over the 2027 budget, which aims to cut a deficit tied to debt near 120% of GDP, are pushing up the risk premium across maturities.
fr5y.outlook: Bias higher while the budget is unresolved; range 4.30–4.50%. A calm weekend and progress on the bill would ease pressure.
fr5y.watch: Saturday's protests and the budget debate from Oct 27.

fr10y.note: Closed near 5.01%, up about 8–9bp, after a 5.022% high; OAT–Bund spread about 158bp.
fr10y.why: The 10-year OAT closed above 5% for the first time since July 2002 and is up more than 20bp this week, the sharpest rise among major markets. Riots at the weekend, more protests called for Saturday and an indecisive revenue vote have revived doubts about fiscal consolidation, while far-right and far-left candidates lead 2027 polls. Bunds rose only 3bp, so the spread neared October's 15-year high of about 159bp.
fr10y.outlook: Spread bias wider in a 150–170bp range until the budget clears. A close above 160bp would open talk of ECB backstops and ratings risk; a calm weekend could pull it back toward 150bp.
fr10y.watch: Protests Saturday Oct 24, the budget debate from Oct 27, the ECB on Oct 29 and rating reviews.

fr30y.note: About 5.53%, up roughly 7–10bp; the long end carries the biggest fiscal premium.
fr30y.why: The 30-year OAT rose with the rest of the curve as investors demanded more to hold long French debt amid protests and budget doubts, with debt service projected to top €91 billion in 2027. It is now testing this month's highs above 5.50%, while German long bonds held near 3.78%.
fr30y.outlook: The most exposed part of the curve. A close above 5.60% would mark a new cycle high; a credible budget deal is needed to turn it.
fr30y.watch: The budget debate, Saturday's protests and long-dated OAT auctions.

watch: Next: the 5-year TIPS auction and jobless claims Thursday, French protests Saturday, the French budget debate and Fed meeting from Oct 27, EIA data Oct 28, the ECB on Oct 29, OPEC+ on Nov 1, the US midterms Nov 3 and the Nov 4 refunding.
